sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the claimant in MVC No.474/2021.
3.
The claimant aged 14 years, student, met with an accident on 10.01.2021 and sustained grievous injures.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition through his natural NC: 2025:KHC-K:7417 HC-KAR father as a minor guardian before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.7,75,000/-.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.1,37,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2- Insurance Company to deposit the same.

4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, the doctor has assessed the disability at 10%, but the Tribunal has taken it only 4%.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meagre.
Further, interest is to be awarded at 9% p.a.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the arguments of both sides.

6. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Hitesh Nagjibhai Patel vs. Bababhai Nagjibhai Rabari & Anr.1, held that, when a minor child suffers a permanent disability, 2025 LiveLaw (SC) 871 NC:
2025:KHC-K:7417 HC-KAR the compensation for the loss of income should be awarded based on the minimum wages of a skilled worker in the relevant place at the time of the accident.

entities.text: Hitesh Nagjibhai Patel vs. Bababhai Nagjibhai Rabari & Anr.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the said decision, this Court also finds it reasonable to award the compensation under loss of future income based on the minimum wages.
The Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has prepared chart basing on the minimum wages pertaining to the concerned years.
Hence, as the appellant met with an accident in the year 2021, his notional income is to be taken at Rs.14,250/- per month.
He was aged 14 years and therefore, the multiplier is to be taken as '15'.
The appellant has sustained grievous injuries on his left thumb as per Exs.P9 and P10 and he was treated in the hospital as an inpatient for 03 days.
He examined the doctor as PW.4 and the doctor has assessed the disability at 18% to the left upper limb.
So, 1/3rd of the same comes to 6%.
The Tribunal erred in taking the same as 4% and it is to be modified.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to consider the NC:
2025:KHC-K:7417 HC-KAR disability at 6%.

Thus, the loss of future earnings would be:
Rs.14,250 x 12 x 15 x 6% = Rs.1,53,900/-.
7.
The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.27,000/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.

8. Further, considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.10,000/- for pain and suffering and loss of amenities and Rs.10,000/- for transportation and extra nourishment.

9. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Pain and suffering & loss of Rs.10,000/-
amenities Medical expenses Rs.27,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.1,53,900/-
Transportation & extra nourishment Rs.10,000/-
Total Rs.2,00,900/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.1,37,000/-
Enhancement: Rs.63,900/-

Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.63,900/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

10. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
( ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.63,900/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
However, as per order dated 09.10.2025, the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 152 days in filing the appeal.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7417 HC-KAR (iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 is permitted to file vakalath within two weeks.
